content: Environmental storytelling via wear: pristine environments read as artificial movie sets; grime, scuff marks, worn steps, overgrown plants and rust imply passage of time and make worlds feel lived-in. Props are 'silent storytellers' - arrangement matters more than count; details should imply who lives there and what they do (crates near market, worn path between well and door). Worn footpaths specifically encode traffic history: path wear where NPCs/players actually walk. Small details are what players remember; the technique is arrangement-with-meaning, not decoration density. Sources: toxigon.com, beyondextent.com, medium.com John Mulholland, garagefarm.net.
